inputs.original_text: ISRAEL’S parliament began a debate today on a Bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. The Bill’s passage would be a victory for Israel’s far-right Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of the religious party that introduced the legislation. Opponents of the legislation call it racist, draconian and unlikely to deter attacks by Palestinian militants.
inputs.modified_text: Israel's parliament has started debating a bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. This represents a clear victory for far-right Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir and the religious party behind it, and it exposes yet another layer of institutional racism and structural discrimination against Palestinians. These communities already endure deep historical inequalities and systemic oppression, and this draconian measure targets them specifically based on ethnicity rather than addressing the root causes of conflict and injustice. Opponents are right that it amounts to blatant discrimination and will do nothing to protect vulnerable groups or promote real reform.
